security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation syntax, official Microsoft endpoints, private or sample addresses, and SSH public-key references. Fourteen static findings remain confirmed because they contact a third party or change remote firewall, authentication, privilege, networking, or SELinux state. Semantic review also found shell injection exposure, fail-open ingress, unsafe host-key guidance, broad unconfirmed EMM changes, and plaintext password handling.

remediation.issue: User-controlled GitHub delivery values enter shell commands without complete validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist repository and branch formats, resolve target paths inside the checkout, and pass every value as a structured argument instead of shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: Public IP detection failure can produce an unrestricted SSH or RDP source.
remediation.suggestion: Fail closed when detection fails. Require the user to provide and confirm a trusted CIDR before generating or applying any management-port rule.

remediation.issue: Remote remediation and subscription-wide EMM operations can change security controls or incur costs.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact target, commands, scope, and expected impact, then require explicit confirmation immediately before every state-changing operation.

remediation.issue: SSH recovery guidance removes a stored host key without verifying the replacement.
remediation.suggestion: Retrieve the expected host fingerprint through a trusted Azure channel and compare it before removing or replacing any known_hosts entry.

remediation.issue: Windows administrator passwords are placed directly in command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use a secure prompt, protected parameter file, Key Vault reference, or managed identity flow that keeps passwords out of history and process arguments.

remediation.issue: Public IP discovery depends on a third-party ifconfig.me request.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before the lookup and offer a manual CIDR value or an Azure-owned discovery method that avoids disclosing metadata to a third party.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated shell placeholders in GitHub delivery
semantic_findings.description: The workflow accepts user-supplied repository, branch, and target path values, then inserts them into shell commands without validation or consistent quoting. Crafted values could execute unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The same file collects user-controlled branch and path values and later places those placeholders in shell command positions. No allowlist validation or complete shell quoting is specified.

semantic_findings.title: Fail-open management port exposure
semantic_findings.description: The beginner flow permits an unrestricted source when public IP detection fails. This can expose SSH or RDP management ports to the entire internet.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance explicitly allows a wildcard source after detection failure. A warning in the Plan Card does not prevent generation of the exposed configuration.

semantic_findings.title: SSH host key removal lacks fingerprint verification
semantic_findings.description: The SSH troubleshooting table recommends removing the old known_hosts entry after redeployment without first verifying the replacement host key. This can normalize a man-in-the-middle warning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line directly maps host-key verification failure to deleting the stored entry and provides no fingerprint validation step. The omission is security-relevant even in a legitimate redeployment.

semantic_findings.title: Subscription-wide EMM changes lack a final confirmation gate
semantic_findings.description: The EMM flow registers providers and submits a subscription-level deployment on the user behalf without an explicit final confirmation. Enrollment affects existing VMs and can enable paid services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow states that Copilot performs commands and API calls, then reaches provider registration and PUT or DELETE operations without a final approval instruction. The documented scope and pricing effects are subscription-wide.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext passwords in command arguments
semantic_findings.description: Creator and troubleshooting guidance place VM administrator passwords directly in command arguments. These secrets can remain in shell history, transcripts, or process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited command passes a password through an az CLI argument. Command-line secrets can be retained in shell history and exposed through process inspection.

content.user_title: Plan, Deploy, and Troubleshoot Azure Compute
content.value_statement: Azure compute decisions and deployment workflows can be complex and risky. This skill guides VM selection, validation, provisioning, capacity reservations, management enrollment, and connectivity troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Azure VM and VMSS families for stated workloads.
Compares public Azure retail pricing across sizes and regions.
Validates SKU availability, image support, regional support, and vCPU quota.
Generates Azure CLI, Bicep, and Terraform deployment artifacts.
Creates VMs or VM scale sets through Azure MCP after confirmation.
Guides capacity reservations, EMM enrollment, and RDP or SSH troubleshooting.
limitations: Live checks and operations require Azure authentication, permissions, and connected MCP or CLI tools.
Retail price estimates may exclude negotiated discounts, taxes, reservations, and ancillary services.
The creator covers bare VM and VMSS infrastructure, not application deployment.
Generated artifacts and remediation commands can create costs or alter VM security controls.

use_cases.title: Standardize VM deployment
use_cases.description: Create a reviewed Azure CLI, Bicep, or Terraform artifact with validated region, image, SKU, quota, and network settings.

use_cases.title: Compare capacity and cost
use_cases.description: Evaluate VM families, VMSS options, retail prices, quota, and capacity reservations before selecting an architecture.

use_cases.title: Restore VM connectivity
use_cases.description: Diagnose RDP or SSH failures using ordered checks for VM state, networking, guest services, firewall rules, and credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend a development VM
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an Azure VM for a small Linux development server in eastus. Compare two sizes, estimate monthly cost, and explain your choice.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Bicep deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bicep plan for an Ubuntu VM in westeurope. Restrict SSH to my trusted CIDR and validate SKU, image, and quota first.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an SSH timeout
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot an SSH timeout for my Azure VM. Start with read-only checks and request approval before changing networking, firewall, credentials, or SELinux.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production VMSS
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production VMSS for a stateless service. Compare orchestration, autoscale, zones, cost, quota, security, and capacity reservation options.

output_examples.input: Recommend a low-cost Linux VM for development in eastus.
output: Primary option: a general-purpose burstable size for intermittent development workloads.
Alternative: a D-series size for sustained CPU and memory use.
Includes retail cost, quota status, availability notes, and selection tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Create a secure Ubuntu VM with Bicep.
output_examples.output: A reviewed deployment plan followed by Bicep and usage guidance. The plan records region, SKU, image, quota, trusted SSH source, disk, identity, and estimated cost.

output_examples.input: My Azure VM rejects SSH connections.
output_examples.output: An ordered diagnosis covering VM health, public addressing, NSG rules, routes, guest firewall, SSH service, and authentication. State-changing fixes are separated from read-only checks.

best_practices: Validate region, image, SKU, quota, and estimated cost before generating or applying infrastructure.
Restrict SSH and RDP to explicit trusted CIDR ranges, or use private access and Azure Bastion.
Review every state-changing command and confirm the target subscription, resource group, VM, and expected impact.
anti_patterns: Do not use wildcard management-port sources when public IP detection fails.
Do not place passwords, private keys, or other credentials in prompts or command-line arguments.
Do not run firewall, account, networking, SELinux, or subscription changes without explicit approval.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy an application?
faq.answer: No. It covers bare VM and VMSS infrastructure and routes application deployment requests to an application-focused workflow.

faq.question: Which deployment formats are supported?
faq.answer: It can produce Azure CLI, Bicep, or Terraform artifacts. It also supports live VM and VMSS creation through Azure MCP.

faq.question: Does it verify Azure availability and quota?
faq.answer: Yes, when Azure MCP or authenticated CLI access is available. Otherwise, it reports that preflight validation is reduced.

faq.question: Are cost estimates exact?
faq.answer: No. Estimates use public retail pricing and may exclude discounts, reservations, taxes, bandwidth, storage, and related services.

faq.question: Can it change an existing VM?
faq.answer: Yes. Troubleshooting guidance includes commands that can change firewall, credentials, networking, services, or SELinux and therefore require careful approval.

faq.question: What access is required for live operations?
faq.answer: The user must authenticate to Azure and hold permissions for the selected subscription, resource group, and requested operation.
